# Errors and validation

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **Never swallow an exception or error. A catch block must handle, translate, log or rethrow it. A catch that ignores an exception on purpose needs a comment saying why that is safe, or must write the error to a warning or verbose stream. Never write `async void`.** A swallowed error hides a failure the change should surface, and an `async void` method crashes the process or loses its exception. *Check:* Look for empty catch blocks, catch-all handlers that only return a default, `catch { $null = $_ }`, ignored error results and `async void` methods in the diff, where nothing logs the error and no comment explains it. <sub>Identity .github/agents/copilot-reviewer.agent.md; identity-platform .claude/commands/review-plan-diff.md; identity-platform .github/agents/copilot-reviewer.agent.md; project-template .claude/commands/review-plan-diff.md; project-template .github/agents/copilot-reviewer.agent.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; project-template outcomes of #183</sub>
- **When translating exceptions into a domain exception (such as `CryptographicException`, an invalid-key result or a protocol error), catch only the exception types the wrapped operation documents for bad input or for the specific refusal, and let every other exception propagate unchanged.** A broad filter turns bugs, outages, authorization failures, `PlatformNotSupportedException` or `OutOfMemoryException` into a domain failure such as a wrong key, and callers then act on it wrongly, sometimes by destroying data. *Check:* Look for `catch (Exception)`, `when ex is not ...` filters, or catches of `RpcException`/`RequestFailedException` and other broad types that rethrow as a domain exception or return false. Also look for `PlatformNotSupportedException` merged into an invalid-key path, and destructive self-heal or reset code that runs on anything other than the one exception that proves the data is unreadable. <sub>Identity outcomes of #692; Identity ADR-1260; Identity ADR-1247; Identity ADR-1068; Identity ADR-1012</sub>
- **Decide a precondition (exists, unique, has no dependents) from a fact the code queried before the write, and answer 404 or 409 from that read. Never infer it by catching a broad exception such as `InvalidOperationException` or `DbUpdateException`, or from a store write's return value. Catch only the specific exception that signals a race, such as a unique or foreign-key violation, and let other store exceptions propagate as a 500.** Stores report a duplicate, a missing row and a backing-database failure alike with broad exceptions. Mapping them turns a store fault into a misleading conflict, hides the real cause, and can set off compensating actions such as destroying a newly created external key. *Check:* Look for try/catch around store add, save or delete calls in handlers that returns NotFound or Conflict for a general exception type, for 404/409 chosen from the result of a write, and for conflict checks that run only after side-effecting calls. <sub>Identity ADR-1424; Identity ADR-1483; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity outcomes of #686</sub>
- **Map a refused or invalid input to a 400 only through a dedicated exception type or result, plus the exceptions a dependency documents as refusals. Let every other exception, including broad types such as `InvalidOperationException`, `ArgumentException` and `CryptographicException`, reach the logged 5xx path.** Catching broad types as a 400 turns SDK, client or misconfiguration faults into unlogged bad requests and leaks the raw exception message into the problem detail. *Check:* Look for catch clauses or filters that map broad exception types to a bad-request response when the called API does not document them as refusals. <sub>Identity outcomes of #699</sub>
- **Let an `OperationCanceledException` caused by the caller's token, or by `HttpContext.RequestAborted`, propagate unchanged. Never turn it into an error response, a failure result, a retry, an error log or an audit write, and never report it as a timeout.** Cancellation means the caller or client went away. It is not a fault of the server, the provider or the input. *Check:* Look for catch blocks that swallow `OperationCanceledException` into a failure result, a 500, a protocol error, an audit write or a retry, and for code that treats every `OperationCanceledException` as a timeout without checking whether the caller's token was cancelled. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-1167; Identity ADR-1274; Identity ADR-1280; Identity ADR-1285; Identity ADR-1290; Identity ADR-1315; Identity ADR-1336</sub>
- **Make a value a remote party sends that is invalid, malformed or hostile fail with the endpoint's defined client error (400, `invalid_request` or the protocol's own error code), never with an unhandled exception that becomes a 500. Map strict-encoding failures (`DecoderFallbackException`, `EncoderFallbackException`) to that error, or to the exception type the method's contract documents, instead of substituting characters or letting them escape.** A remote party controls these values, so any throwing parse, conversion, decode or arithmetic lets every caller trigger a server error instead of a defined rejection. *Check:* Look for parsing, decoding or arithmetic on untrusted claims, parameters, headers or response bodies that can throw without being mapped to the client error, for replacement fallbacks on strict encodings, and for try blocks that catch only HTTP, cancellation or JSON exceptions around strict decoding. <sub>Identity ADR-1123; Identity ADR-1266; Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Make a value that is present but invalid fail closed. Never treat a malformed field, header, directive or setting as absent, and refuse a parameter, option or request field the code does not honor with a 400 or an error instead of accepting it and dropping it silently.** Silently ignoring malformed or unsupported input hides errors, weakens security, and returns success although the caller's intent was not applied. *Check:* Look for parse failures that fall back to the 'not provided' path, a present but non-matching directive line that falls through to the no-directive behaviour, and handler branches that validate a field and then build the downstream request without it while still returning success. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity ADR-1403; Identity outcomes of #551; project-template outcomes of #149</sub>
- **Make a correctness or security control that relies on a shared store (brute-force or failed-attempt limits, replay detection, session lookup) fail closed: let the store's exception propagate, and never read an unreachable store or a degenerate operation (such as an expiry that is not in the future) as success, absent or new. Make a capacity guard such as a rate limiter fail open instead: bound each store call with a short timeout, use a circuit breaker that admits requests without calling the store while it is open, log a warning, and don't bill overage the counter did not see.** An outage of the shared state must not lift a security control, but it must not take the service down through a capacity guard either. *Check:* In security limiters and replay checks, look for try/catch around store calls that returns 'not limited', success or absent. In capacity limiters, look for store exceptions that refuse the request, store calls with no short timeout, missing breaker logic, failures swallowed without a warning, or recorded overage. <sub>Identity ADR-1237; Identity ADR-1164; Identity ADR-1246; Identity ADR-1198</sub>
- **When a session or shared-state store is unavailable, translate its exceptions into a dedicated store-unavailable failure answered with 503. Never answer 401, treat the request as anonymous, sign the user out, or treat the session as missing.** A store outage is not proof that the user is unauthenticated, and a 401 logs users out or sends frontends into a login loop while hiding the outage. *Check:* Look at catch blocks and error paths around session-store reads and lease operations that return 401, an anonymous principal or a sign-out, or that fall through to a challenge. <sub>Identity ADR-1290; Identity ADR-1292; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **Never let date and time arithmetic overflow. Range-check before `DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds`, saturate at `DateTimeOffset.MaxValue` or `MinValue` when adding or subtracting a margin, lifetime or configurable clock skew, or compare elapsed time instead (`now - issuedAt - skew > maxAge`).** A received far-future instant or a configured `TimeSpan.MaxValue` meaning 'no limit' makes these operations throw, which escapes result-returning APIs or wrongly refuses every token. *Check:* Look for `FromUnixTimeSeconds` on untrusted input, `instant + margin`, `Add*`, `now + skew` or `MaxAge + ClockSkew` on received or configurable values without a saturation guard, and for missing tests of the extreme skew. <sub>Identity ADR-1123; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity outcomes of #552; Identity outcomes of #554</sub>
- **Check `ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Object` before reading members of JSON parsed from wire input, and in production code read `JsonElement` members through the repository's shared non-throwing helpers where it has them, rather than hand-rolled `TryGetProperty` + `ValueKind` + `Get*` chains.** `TryGetProperty` throws `InvalidOperationException` on a non-object, and the bare getters throw on a mismatched kind, so untrusted input could fault the caller. *Check:* Look for `TryGetProperty`/`GetProperty` on parsed token headers, payloads or request bodies with no preceding object check, and for `GetString()`/`GetInt64()` chains, bare `JsonValueKind.Null` absence checks or re-parsing "{}" where a shared helper exists. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **After deserializing a request body, check every property that must not be null, `required` ones included, and answer 400 with a validation problem before passing it to code that throws `ArgumentNullException`.** In System.Text.Json, `required` only checks that the property is present, so an explicit JSON null passes (unless `RespectNullableAnnotations` is on), reaches a guard clause, and the client gets a 500 for bad input. *Check:* Look for request DTOs with `required` or non-nullable reference properties whose handler passes them on without a null check, especially where a refactor replaced a null-tolerant comparison with a helper that calls `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull`. <sub>Identity outcomes of #724; Identity outcomes of #827</sub>
- **In an ASP.NET Core endpoint, read a form body once, up front, through the repository's single shared try-read helper, and answer the `InvalidDataException` that `ReadFormAsync` throws for a malformed or oversized body with the endpoint's usual 400 invalid-request error.** Uncaught, a client input error becomes a 500 and an error log entry, and duplicated readers drift apart. *Check:* Look for direct `ReadFormAsync` calls with no catch for `InvalidDataException`, local copies of the try-read helper, or form reads after client authentication. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity outcomes of #464</sub>
- **Make a Try-pattern method that reports refusals as `false` check whether the input is supported before calling anything that can throw for unsupported input, or catch the exception types the callee documents. It must never let an exception escape for input the caller sent.** An exception out of a Try method breaks the contract callers rely on and turns a refusal into a 500. *Check:* In new `Try*` code, look for calls that run before the supported-type check, and for catch filters that leave out exceptions the callee documents, such as `NotSupportedException`. <sub>Identity outcomes of #757</sub>
- **Bound the work untrusted input can demand with configurable limits (input size, item count, nesting depth, number of signatures or recipients), check them before or while decoding rather than after, validate the limit options when the host starts, and reject cheaply any value that doesn't have the exact expected shape, such as a fixed-length handle, before lookups or cryptography.** The sender controls how much work parsing takes, and a strict shape check rejects attacker-chosen values cheaply. *Check:* Look for count or depth checks that run only after decoding, CBOR readers not in `CborConformanceMode.Strict` or without size, trailing-byte, indefinite-length, label-type, depth and count checks, limit options without startup validation, and handles passed to a KDF or store without a length check. <sub>Identity ADR-1405; Identity ADR-1409; Identity ADR-1290</sub>
- **Make a producer (issuer, encoder, signer) enforce the same structural limits its consumers enforce (nesting depth, element counts, reserved names), and refuse input beyond them with `ArgumentException`.** Otherwise the producer signs output that every later verification step rejects. *Check:* Compare the limit checks in an issuer or encoder with those in the matching holder or verifier, and report any limit only one side enforces. <sub>Identity outcomes of #552; Identity ADR-1405</sub>
- **End a .NET or PowerShell regular expression that validates a whole value with `\z`, not `$`.** In .NET and PowerShell `$` also matches before a trailing newline, so `^[a-z]+$` accepts `"acme\n"`, which can then reach a command or other sensitive sink. *Check:* Look for whole-value validation patterns of the form `^...$` in `Regex`, `[RegularExpression]` or PowerShell `-match` without options that change `$`. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; project-template outcomes of #124; project-template outcomes of #146</sub>
- **Match digits with `[0-9]`, not `\d`, in a .NET or PowerShell regex that validates or extracts a number passed on to another system (an API path, a CLI argument, an identifier).** .NET `\d` also matches non-ASCII Unicode digits, so malformed input passes validation and fails later with misleading state. *Check:* Look for `\d` in regexes that parse numbers, IDs or counts for later use, unless the pattern uses `RegexOptions.ECMAScript` or is meant to accept Unicode digits. <sub>project-template outcomes of #268</sub>
- **Use `Debug.Assert` only for internal invariants. Throw for anything derived from parsed, caller-supplied or external input.** `Debug.Assert` is compiled out of Release builds, so bad input is accepted in production. *Check:* Look for `Debug.Assert` on arguments, parsed values or external data. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **Validate a configured value the way it will be used, and reject one that parses to something other than what was written. `IPAddress.TryParse`, `IPNetwork.TryParse` and `Uri.TryCreate` are lenient: require canonical IPv4, CIDR whose address is the network's first address, absolute URIs with an explicit `scheme:` and no whitespace, and keep a value compared verbatim (such as a CORS origin, validated as a browser Origin with no path, query, user info or trailing slash) in the form it is compared in. Validate enums with `Enum.IsDefined`.** Lenient parsers turn typos into other values (shorthand and octal IPv4, implicit file paths, normalized URIs), and the configuration binder reads enums from numbers. *Check:* Look for options validation that relies only on `TryParse`/`TryCreate` success, origins stored normalized, enum options without `Enum.IsDefined`, and CORS or forwarded-header options bound without a validator. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-1447; Identity ADR-1370</sub>
- **Give a rule that guards data one implementation and call it from every path that accepts or consumes that data: startup configuration and reload, API writes, imports, registration, seeders, alternative runners and stored data on read. Reject an invalid value with the same outcome at each, and express a cross-setting consistency requirement as a registered rule a shared validator runs, not as a check inside one caller.** A check that only one path runs lets another path store or execute what the first refuses. *Check:* Look for validation added to one entry path (for example config binding) while another path that writes, loads or executes the same value skips it, and for consistency checks written inline in one endpoint or seeder. <sub>Identity ADR-1140; Identity ADR-1139; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; project-template outcomes of #149</sub>
- **In production code, give every validated setting a domain rule as well as its type (a closed string set is one-of, lifetimes are at least one second, timeouts are positive, lists check each element and reject null elements), and validate a value a renderer or other consumer reads against the exact shape it reads (for example `#rgb`/`#rrggbb` colors, absolute `https` image URIs, bounded text without control characters).** A value of the right type that the server can't honor slips through and fails later, at render or request time. *Check:* Look for new setting descriptors or options without a domain rule, lists validated as a whole but not element by element, and presentation settings that accept free-form values. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-1140; Identity ADR-1253</sub>
- **Reject input that names an unregistered member of a vocabulary (a strategy, profile, provider, method or format) instead of ignoring it, returning a no-op or falling back to a default.** An open vocabulary is still closed to unregistered input; an unknown name otherwise silently runs without the behaviour it was configured for. *Check:* Look for lookups by name that skip unknown names, return null, an empty result or a default, or continue when nothing is registered. <sub>Identity ADR-1150; Identity ADR-1140; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-1190</sub>
- **Validate a registered set of named descriptors, handlers or strategies as a whole when it is composed: throw an exception that names the offending entry for a null entry, a null, empty or whitespace name (`string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace`), a duplicate name or selector, a dangling reference or a cycle. Compare names ordinally, build the lookup once, and order entries deterministically with an ordinal tiebreak.** A misregistration should fail at composition with a clear message, not when a request first uses it, and a duplicate must never silently win. *Check:* Look for registries built with `ToDictionary` or indexer overwrites, last-wins or first-wins behaviour, linear searches per call, culture-sensitive or case-insensitive name comparison, `IsNullOrEmpty` on codes, loops that dereference entries without a null check, and exceptions that don't name the entry. <sub>Identity ADR-1119; Identity ADR-1150; Identity ADR-1190; Identity ADR-1201; Identity ADR-1246; Identity ADR-1392; Identity ADR-1474; Identity ADR-1145; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity outcomes of #532</sub>
- **Reject a settings document that cannot be honored wherever it enters the system: an unregistered name, a value the binder cannot convert, a list written as a scalar or the reverse, a document that is not a JSON object, null for a setting with no default, or an entry valid by name and value that sits at a scope that never reads it. Never load it partially, store it, skip the bad entry or drop it on write. Validate a document written through an API before storing it, answer 400 keyed by setting name, and store nothing.** Configuration accepted without being honored is an invisible failure, and a skipped security control is one the operator configured but the server doesn't enforce. *Check:* Look for settings parsing that ignores unknown or out-of-scope keys, catches conversion failures and continues, treats a non-object as `{}`, accepts scalar/list mismatches, or persists before validating. An empty array must configure an empty list, not be rejected. <sub>Identity ADR-1139; Identity ADR-1149</sub>
- **Validate configuration that would otherwise fail on first use (unknown strategy codes, route templates missing a required parameter, uncompilable patterns, malformed URLs, limit options) before the host starts, for example with `ValidateOnStart`, not on the request path or inside a hosted service after startup.** A late failure comes after health checks report the instance ready, or faults one background service while the rest of the host keeps serving. *Check:* Look for options checked or parsed lazily on the request path or in a hosted service's run loop, and options bound without `ValidateOnStart`. <sub>Identity ADR-1137; Identity ADR-1370; Identity ADR-1405</sub>
- **Make a start-time check over several independent conditions or items collect every failure and throw one `InvalidOperationException` that lists them all, run before any resource starts, without an opt-out switch.** A host with several problems would otherwise need one restart per problem, and one report lets a single repair fix everything. *Check:* Look for startup validation loops that throw on the first malformed or duplicate entry, or checks that run after resources have started or add a bypass flag. <sub>Identity ADR-1071; Identity ADR-1433; Identity ADR-1504; Identity outcomes of #548</sub>
- **Make a configuration or startup failure message start with the full configuration key path of the member (such as `Section:Item:Member must ...`) in the validator's one consistent format, name the failing item, state the constraint, and name the call or command that repairs it when there is one. Quote the rejected value only when it cannot carry a secret, build thresholds from the constant rather than a literal, and show a configured URL without user info, query or fragment.** An operator must find the exact key that stopped the host, but configured values can be passwords or credentials, and messages end up in logs. *Check:* Look for validation messages that omit the key path or failing item, interpolate a bound value that could be secret (passwords, connection strings, URIs with `@`), contain literal threshold numbers, or use a format different from sibling messages. *Note:* Sources conflict on including the value: ADR-1137 and outcomes of #506/#531 ask for it, ADR-1509/ADR-1510 forbid it, and outcomes of #709 says naming the key and constraint is enough. Don't report a message for lacking the value when it names the full key path and constraint; do report a message that echoes a possibly secret value. <sub>Identity ADR-1137; Identity ADR-1509; Identity ADR-1510; Identity outcomes of #506; Identity outcomes of #531; Identity outcomes of #598; Identity outcomes of #606; Identity outcomes of #709; Identity ADR-1433; Identity ADR-1071; Identity ADR-1238; Identity ADR-1439</sub>
- **When a message rejects a value that must come from a known set (registered names, algorithms, providers, formats), list the accepted values, ordinally sorted, or say that none are registered.** Otherwise a caller or operator with a mistyped value gets no hint and must look the valid values up elsewhere. *Check:* Look for rejection messages for enum-like or registered values that name only the bad value. <sub>Identity outcomes of #532; Identity outcomes of #686; Identity ADR-1104</sub>
- **After a change has committed, run each follow-up step (announcement, cache eviction, refresh, audit publish, notification, session termination, counter reset) in its own catch that logs the failure and continues with the remaining steps. Never let a step's failure, or a timeout from its own bound, fail the already-committed operation.** The change is durable; an error response would make the caller retry a change that already happened, and one failed step would skip the others. *Check:* Look for post-commit step sequences without per-step exception handling, steps whose exception reaches the caller, back-to-back cache evictions where the first failing skips the second, and failures swallowed without a log. <sub>Identity ADR-1205; Identity ADR-1351; Identity ADR-1404; Identity outcomes of #551; Identity outcomes of #555</sub>
- **When a loop commits destructive changes one item at a time, or a committed delete leaves external resources to destroy, run the side effects for what is already committed (eviction, notifications, audit, destroying external resources such as KMS keys) in a `finally` or before any step that can fail or be cancelled. Run cleanup of external resources on its own bounded token, not the request's, and log each failure with the identifiers needed to reclaim it.** Otherwise a later failure or a client disconnect leaves deleted items cached and unannounced, or leaves an external key live with nothing pointing to it. *Check:* Look for evict, notify, audit or destroy calls placed only after a per-item loop or after audit calls on the request's cancellation token, outside a `finally`, and for cleanup failures logged without the key or record id and provider. <sub>Identity outcomes of #553; Identity outcomes of #647; Identity ADR-1478; Identity ADR-1205</sub>
- **Dispatch to several observers, audit sinks or handlers so that each runs in its own try/catch that logs its failure: one handler's failure must not stop the others, reach the publisher, or change the audited operation's response.** Observation must not alter outcomes, and a slow or failing sink must not break the operation or the other sinks. *Check:* Look for loops that await handlers without a per-handler catch and log, and for audit or publish calls in response paths that can throw into the response. <sub>Identity ADR-1047; Identity ADR-1205; Identity docs/audit-records.md</sub>
- **In a `BackgroundService` or timer-driven loop, catch every exception from a run, `OperationCanceledException` included, unless the service's own stopping token is cancelled; log it with a dedicated event and retry at the next tick or after a delay instead of letting it escape `ExecuteAsync`.** An escaping exception faults the service: under `BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior.StopHost` the host stops, otherwise the work never runs again. *Check:* Look at `ExecuteAsync` or `PeriodicTimer` loops that catch only specific types, or that catch `OperationCanceledException` without checking `stoppingToken`. <sub>Identity ADR-1218; Identity ADR-1443; Identity outcomes of #608</sub>
- **In a background or batch pass over many independent items (records, tenants, owners, providers), put all per-item work, store reads included, inside a per-item try/catch that lets cancellation of the stopping token propagate, logs the item's identity (tenant and record id), skips the item without serving or reinterpreting it, and continues. Keep any broader catch only around setup, and report the pass as incomplete when an item failed so it is retried.** One malformed item that throws out of the loop aborts every pass at the same place, so the valid items after it are never processed and the same failure is logged forever. *Check:* Look for one try/catch around the whole iteration, awaited per-item calls placed before the per-item try, catches that don't name the item, and exceptions that end the loop. *Note:* A concurrency conflict in a pass run by several replicas at once (rows already removed by another replica) counts as progress, not failure. <sub>Identity ADR-1223; Identity ADR-1395; Identity ADR-1407; Identity ADR-1412; Identity ADR-1443; Identity ADR-1199; Identity outcomes of #545; Identity outcomes of #577; Identity outcomes of #599; Identity outcomes of #608; Identity outcomes of #702</sub>
- **Scope each try block to the operation its catch handles and its log message names. Keep decoding and parsing of a fetched body outside the catch that maps transport failures, and give follow-up work its own try, so each failure is reported with the code and message of the part that actually failed.** A broad try reports a malformed document as a network failure, logs follow-up failures under the wrong message, and points the operator at the wrong component. *Check:* Look for catches whose message or error code describes one input or operation while the try also covers others, including lazily evaluated `JsonNode` conversions, decoding, or loops over removals. <sub>Identity outcomes of #552; Identity outcomes of #577; Identity outcomes of #825</sub>
- **On the request path, let a stored record that cannot be read fail the request that reads it, list endpoints included; never skip it in a listing, default its missing members, or fall back to another interpretation. Report a load failure with a message naming the owner and the record.** A listing that silently skips a record looks complete while hiding data the store holds, and a guessed default for a malformed record can keep something alive or authorize it. *Check:* Look for catch-and-continue or filter-out logic around deserializing stored records in request code, and for readers that default or skip missing required members instead of throwing. *Note:* Background passes with no caller log and skip instead (see the per-item rule). A best-effort derived field added to a management response may be omitted when its stored source is unreadable, so that the operator can still find the broken resource. <sub>Identity ADR-1395; Identity ADR-1220; Identity ADR-1471; Identity ADR-1289</sub>
- **Never fall back to reading protected stored data as plaintext, and never silently delete or regenerate a persisted key that cannot be unprotected outside an explicit development opt-in. A protected payload that fails to unprotect with `CryptographicException` is treated as absent and logged as a warning; a key that cannot be unprotected fails the load with a message naming its owner.** A plaintext fallback accepts a forged row, and regenerating an unreadable key hides a lost key and changes the keys relying parties trust. *Check:* Look for unprotect calls whose failure falls through to plaintext deserialization, is swallowed without a log, or triggers deletion or regeneration of key material. <sub>Identity ADR-1235; Identity ADR-1169</sub>
- **When more than one candidate matches (selection rules, tenants for a host, conflicting opt-ins such as a confidential-body mark plus body logging), fail closed instead of picking one: throw a clear exception at build or composition time, or resolve to 'no match' on the request path and report the conflict.** Picking one arbitrarily binds the request to the wrong client, tenant or setting, or quietly logs credentials. *Check:* Look for `FirstOrDefault` over possibly multiple matches without ambiguity detection, `Single` that throws a 500 per request, and convention code that silently lets one conflicting setting win. <sub>Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity ADR-1165; Identity ADR-1503</sub>
- **When a required configured value (such as an issuer) is missing, fail with an error that names the setting to configure; never substitute a value derived from the request (its scheme and host) or a hard-coded guess.** A request-derived fallback is an unvalidated second source of the same value and makes the result depend on the request. *Check:* Look for null-coalescing or fallback branches that use the request origin or a literal when the configured value is missing. <sub>Identity ADR-1165; Identity ADR-1182</sub>
- **Make a filtered bulk update, revoke or delete throw `ArgumentException` (or answer 400) when its filter is empty, give its criteria type an emptiness check, and count every new filter field toward it.** An empty filter would act on every record. *Check:* Look at bulk methods taking a filter or criteria object for a missing emptiness guard, or a new field not included in it. <sub>Identity ADR-1080; Identity ADR-1222; Identity ADR-1020</sub>
- **Run request validation, length checks against the persisted column (using a constant shared with the column configuration), ordering checks and local conflict checks (such as a duplicate identifier answering 409) before any expensive or side-effecting external call, before generating key material, and before reading rows in a batch.** An invalid request must not cost a remote round trip, create remote resources that need cleanup, or do partial work before failing at the store with a 500. *Check:* Look for external create, read or prove calls, key generation or per-row loops that run before the validator, duplicate check or precondition; and for column limits duplicated as separate literals. <sub>Identity ADR-1476; Identity ADR-1471; Identity ADR-1403; Identity ADR-1408; Identity outcomes of #572</sub>
- **When code creates an external resource (such as a KMS key) and then checks what the service returned, return the resource's identifier as soon as it exists and treat any failure afterwards, including parse or import errors and cancellation, as a failed check: hand the resource to one central destroyer and throw the documented exception type with the original as inner exception. Make destroy succeed when the resource is already missing, disabled or scheduled for deletion.** An unguarded check that throws before cleanup leaks a billable, sensitive resource that nothing references, and cleanup must be safe to repeat during sweeps and rollback. *Check:* Look for checks or awaits between creation and returning the identifier, verification steps whose `CryptographicException`/`ArgumentException`/`FormatException` escapes without cleanup, and destroy implementations that throw on not-found. <sub>Identity ADR-1471; Identity ADR-1474; Identity outcomes of #647</sub>
- **Answer validation failures with distinct statuses: 400 for a value invalid on its own, checked before 409 for a conflict with another resource or with stored state the caller can repair (naming the item to repair, never 422 or a 500), 404 for a missing parent or target, and 412 for a failed or malformed `If-Match`. Report validation results as structured values that keep these kinds apart.** Callers must tell a malformed value from one another resource holds, a server fault from a state they can fix, and a failed precondition from a bad request. *Check:* Look for validators returning plain strings for every kind of failure, endpoints mapping all failures to one status, conflicts checked before value validity, repairable stored-state errors escaping as 500, and malformed `If-Match` answered 400. <sub>Identity ADR-1160; Identity ADR-1245; Identity ADR-1026; Identity ADR-1513</sub>
- **Surface a lost optimistic-concurrency race as a store-neutral concurrency exception: the persistence layer translates Entity Framework's `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` into it with the original as inner exception, a store's own token comparison throws the same type, and code outside the persistence layer never catches EF types. Map it to 412 once, in an endpoint filter on the API's root route group, not in each handler.** Callers must not depend on one store technology, and a handler that forgets a local catch answers 500. *Check:* Look for `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` or `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore` references outside the persistence layer, token mismatches that throw another type or return false, and per-handler catches or 412 answers built from the concurrency exception. <sub>Identity ADR-1012; Identity ADR-1483</sub>
- **Map a cross-cutting exception to its HTTP answer in one endpoint filter on the root route group, and build an error response that more than one place returns (the same not-found, the shared authentication-required 401) through one shared factory, using the same wording wherever the same misconfiguration is detected.** Answers written in separate handlers drift apart, and a handler added later forgets the catch or rewords the message. *Check:* Look for handlers catching an exception a root-group filter already maps, per-handler try/catch that produce problem responses, error messages duplicated inline, and different wording for the same condition in an options validator and a runtime check. <sub>Identity ADR-1245; Identity ADR-1067; Identity outcomes of #622; Identity outcomes of #503</sub>
- **Classify failures by a machine-readable failure code set where the failure is detected, and branch on that code or on a structured status, never on the text of an exception message, error description or merged CLI output.** Message text is meant for humans and logs and is not a stable contract, so a decision taken from it breaks silently. *Check:* Look for `Message.Contains`, `StartsWith`, regex or `-match '404'` against error text that decides control flow or maps to error names, and for `Fail` calls or failure results without a code. *Note:* Don't report message matching when the remote API offers no distinguishing field for that case and a failed match only degrades to the existing generic handling. <sub>Identity ADR-1278; Identity ADR-1405; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; project-template outcomes of #129</sub>
- **Let layers above the detection point pass a failure code through unchanged instead of translating it with a mapping table, derive success from it in result types (`IsValid => FailureCode is null`), resolve the default code for unrecognized exceptions in one place, reuse existing code strings for the same meaning, and refuse an empty failure reason (`ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrEmpty`).** A mapping table loses codes it doesn't list, a separate success flag can disagree with the code, and duplicate code strings for one concept break consistency across formats. *Check:* Look for switch statements or dictionaries translating one layer's codes into another's, wrappers that drop the inner code, result types with an `IsValid` field beside a code, scattered fallback codes, new constants duplicating an existing concept, and `Fail` factories without a reason guard. <sub>Identity ADR-1278; Identity ADR-1410; Identity outcomes of #554</sub>
- **When adding a more specific exception for a case already thrown as a base type, derive it from that base type, give it properties that identify the failing item, and keep the original exception as its inner exception.** Existing catch blocks still catch it, and callers can name the failing item without parsing the message. *Check:* Look for a new exception type that replaces a thrown base exception (such as `JsonException`) without deriving from it, without identifying properties, or dropping the original. <sub>Identity ADR-1245; Identity ADR-1012</sub>
- **Don't derive an exception that signals a recoverable unavailability (a revoked or unreachable key, a store outage) from a type that other code treats as permanent corruption and handles by deleting data, such as `CryptographicException`.** Cleanup or pruning code that catches the base type would destroy data while it is only temporarily unavailable. *Check:* Look for new unavailability or transient exception types whose base type is caught by cleanup, heal or pruning code. <sub>Identity ADR-1414</sub>
- **Choose exception types by what the caller should do: `ArgumentException` for a bad argument or mismatched creation input (naming the parameters object for one of its properties), `InvalidOperationException` for a configuration problem or an operation not possible in the current configuration, `NotSupportedException` for an operation never offered, and `IOException` for an integrity failure that is worth retrying.** The type tells callers whether to fix the call, fix configuration, give up or retry. *Check:* Look for stub operations, configuration errors, mismatched factory inputs and checksum mismatches that throw a type other than the one matching their cause, or a protocol exception used for a configuration error. *Note:* Don't ask for `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when the bad value is a property of a parameters or options object; the convention is an `ArgumentException` naming that object. <sub>Identity ADR-1474; Identity ADR-1471; Identity ADR-1285; Identity ADR-1199; Identity outcomes of #554</sub>
- **When a recovery or fallback step runs inside a catch, don't let its exception replace the original: rethrow the original with the recovery failure attached (for example with `ExceptionDispatchInfo` or an `AggregateException`).** Otherwise the logs show the secondary failure instead of the one that caused it. *Check:* Look for catch blocks that call another fallible operation, such as a re-read after a failed insert, without a try around it that keeps the original. <sub>Identity outcomes of #555</sub>

- **Validate an update against the proposed state (the patch applied to a throwaway copy), revalidate configuration-dependent fields only when the update changes them, and report only the violations the change itself introduces: compare before and after, skip the check when none of the settings it reads changed, and log and skip pre-existing invalid stored items instead of letting them block the write.** Row rules must hold for the state that will be stored, and a violation that predates the change, or one bad document, must not block unrelated writes, including the write that would repair it. *Check:* Look for update handlers that validate the stored entity or raw patch, rerun full address or configuration validation on unrelated edits, report existing violations on any write, or let a parse exception from a walk over stored items escape. <sub>Identity ADR-1424; Identity ADR-1160; Identity ADR-1155; Identity ADR-1206; Identity ADR-1245</sub>
- **When an endpoint creates a resource owned by a parent identified only by a route id, load the parent after authorizing and answer 404 if it doesn't exist instead of storing the owner id unchecked.** Authorization on a route-built node doesn't prove it exists; resources owned by a missing parent would pass to whoever later creates a parent with that id. *Check:* Look for create handlers that set a parent id from the route without loading the parent, and for missing tests with an unknown parent. <sub>Identity outcomes of #629</sub>
- **When a grant or similar change is refused, save and audit nothing; when it is already in place, return the existing state and record nothing; record and report creation only when something was added. Run a resource's own extra refusals before the shared flow.** The audit trail must record exactly what changed. *Check:* Look for paths that save or audit on refusal or on an existing assignment, return 201 when nothing was added, or run resource-specific refusals after the shared flow committed. <sub>Identity ADR-1465</sub>
- **Give every outbound call to another service an explicit timeout and bounded retries with random jitter, and handle HTTP 429 throttling from remote services (such as key vaults) with back-off instead of failing on the first throttle.** Without timeouts and with unbounded or synchronized retries a dependency failure spreads into a retry storm, and throttled calls on a hot path must back off. *Check:* Look for `HttpClient` or SDK calls without a timeout, retry loops with no maximum attempt count or jitter, and adapters that surface the first 429 as a failure. <sub>Identity ADR-1134; Identity docs/hosting-analysis.md</sub>
- **Surface a resilience-pipeline timeout on an outbound HTTP call as `HttpClient.Timeout` does, a `TaskCanceledException` with a `TimeoutException` inner exception, and build the pipeline with the registered `TimeProvider`.** Callers tell timeouts from their own cancellation the same way for every client, and the registered `TimeProvider` keeps time testable. *Check:* Look for `TimeoutRejectedException` reaching callers, other exception types for timeouts, and pipelines using `TimeProvider.System` instead of the one from DI. <sub>Identity ADR-1336; Identity ADR-1385</sub>
- **Decide which exceptions count as fetch failures for outbound HTTP calls in one shared predicate covering timeouts, `HttpRequestException`, `IOException` and corrupt or undecompressable bodies (`InvalidDataException`, `InvalidOperationException` from decompression streams), letting the caller's cancellation propagate. - **When resolving a host name with `Dns.GetHostAddressesAsync` and treating an unresolvable name as a non-error, catch `ArgumentException` as well as `SocketException`.** Malformed or overlong names that `System.Uri` accepts make resolution throw `ArgumentException`, which would turn a validation into a 500. *Check:* Look for DNS resolution in a catch that handles only `SocketException`. <sub>Identity outcomes of #825</sub>
- **Don't let a cached lazy creation cache a transient failure: use `LazyThreadSafetyMode.PublicationOnly` for a `Lazy<T>` whose factory can fail transiently, or remove the cache entry when creation fails.** The default `ExecutionAndPublication` mode caches the exception, so the entry stays broken until restart. *Check:* Look for `Lazy<T>` or cached tasks created with the default mode around factories that can throw. <sub>Identity outcomes of #584</sub>
- **When cache revalidation cannot read the current state or an eviction fails, log a dedicated event and fall back to clearing every affected entry and its dependent material.** A full clear is always safe; without it stale entries stay in service. *Check:* Look at revalidation catch paths that swallow the error or keep cached entries. <sub>Identity ADR-1416; Identity outcomes of #555</sub>
- **In production code, never use the null-forgiving operator `!`, even with a comment; restructure with `?? throw`, `[MemberNotNullWhen]`, an `is { } value` pattern, an early return or `Assert.NotNull` in tests.** The compiler should prove non-nullness rather than be silenced, and test projects lack the extended nullable analyzer, so a suppression there hides real mistakes too. *Check:* Look for postfix `!` on expressions and `#pragma warning disable CS86xx` in the diff. *Note:* Test projects may pass `null!` deliberately to the code under test in an argument-validation test; otherwise tests fix nullable warnings properly too. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-testing.instructions.md</sub>
- **Under a `where T : notnull` constraint, don't use `T?` and `is null` as the 'has a value' flag; track presence with a `bool` or constrain to `where T : struct`.** For value types `T?` is plain `T`, only an annotation, so the null check is always false. *Check:* Look for generic `T?` fields or values under a `notnull` constraint tested against null to mean 'unset'. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Null-guard an extension member's receiver and name the receiver as the exception's parameter name, suppressing CA2208 with a tight `#pragma warning disable/restore` and a reason rather than dropping the name.** Extension members can be called on null, and CA2208 doesn't recognize the receiver as a parameter. *Check:* Look for public extension members without an `ArgumentNullException` for a null receiver, or throwing with another parameter name. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Don't discard the `bool` result of a `Try*` call because a comment says it must succeed; check it and return a specific error, or take the value from the resolution that already validated it.** If the assumption ever breaks, the null result causes misleading errors downstream. *Check:* Look for `_ = TryGet...(...)` or ignored `Try*` results justified by a comment. <sub>Identity outcomes of #702</sub>
- **Don't null-check a non-nullable member that always has a default instance; drop the check or make the member's nullability match it.** The check hides the contract that the value is always present. *Check:* Look for `is not null` or `!= null` checks on members declared non-nullable with a default initializer. <sub>Identity outcomes of #606</sub>
- **Resolve a warning by fixing the code first (a nullable local for a `[MaybeNullWhen(false)]` out argument, `Assert.NotNull` before a dereference, a specific exception type instead of `new Exception(...)`). Only then add a per-rule `.editorconfig` entry with a one-line reason, and as a last resort a tight `#pragma warning disable/restore` pair with a reason at a single site.** Suppressions are justified exceptions that must be narrow and explained. *Check:* Look for new pragmas, `SuppressMessage`, `.editorconfig` severity changes or `NoWarn` where a code fix was possible, a disable without a matching restore, a pragma covering more than one site, or a suppression without a reason. <sub>Identity ADR-1127</sub>
- **In an `IBufferWriter<byte>` overload that decodes or parses input, validate the whole input before calling `GetSpan`, `GetMemory` or `Advance`, so malformed input throws without advancing the writer.** Throwing after the writer advanced leaves partial output in the caller's writer. *Check:* Look for writer-based decode methods that request or advance the buffer before validation finishes, or can throw after `Advance`. <sub>Identity review of #375</sub>
- **When cleanup disposes an object and then a resource it depends on, dispose the first inside a try and release the dependent resource in the `finally`.** If the first disposal throws, sequential cleanup skips the second and the resource leaks. *Check:* Look for several related `Dispose()` calls in sequence with no try/finally between them. <sub>project-template outcomes of #189</sub>
- **When replacing content in a document (such as links in an HTML head), keep the original if the replacement has nowhere to be inserted, instead of removing it and adding nothing.** Remove-then-insert with a missing insertion point silently leaves neither version. *Check:* Look for remove-then-insert logic where the insertion point (for example `</head>`) may be missing. <sub>Identity outcomes of #747</sub>
- **When an operation must be applied to every matching item in a collection, process all matches and return only after the loop.** An early return leaves later matches unprocessed while the run reports success. *Check:* Look for `return` or `break` inside loops meant to cover all matches, and for missing tests with two or more matching items. <sub>project-template outcomes of #222</sub>
- **Make template expansion fail and name the leftover tokens when any placeholder remains unreplaced.** A misspelled or new token otherwise passes through as literal text and fails unclearly later. *Check:* Look for template code that replaces tokens one by one and never checks the result for remaining `{{...}}` patterns. <sub>Identity outcomes of #528</sub>
- **When code loads a function, type or member dynamically (by parsing another file, reflection or lookup by name), throw a clear error naming what it expected when the lookup finds nothing.** After a rename or a missing file the lookup otherwise loads nothing or fails later with an unclear null reference. *Check:* Look for `Find`/`GetType`/`GetMethod`-style results used without a null check and descriptive throw. <sub>project-template outcomes of #149</sub>
- **When a probe or check catches exceptions and reports failure, carry the exception type and message, or the timeout, into the failure message.** Without the reason an operator can't tell a protocol mismatch, a refused connection and a timeout apart. *Check:* Look for catches that return null or false and drop the exception, where the caller then reports only that the operation failed. <sub>Identity outcomes of #787</sub>
- **Handle every failure path and edge case of changed code: null, empty, boundary and large inputs, failures and timeouts of external calls, concurrent access, invariant violations and release of acquired resources on every path, and make failures observable. When two paths are meant to behave alike (siblings, read/write, encode/decode), report validation, error handling or logging present in one but missing from the other.** Closing such gaps completes the capability the change delivers, and asymmetry between equivalent paths delivers it inconsistently. *Check:* Compare the changed path with its counterpart for argument validation, failure modes, logging and edge cases; look for parameters used without null or empty handling, unsynchronized shared state, and disposables not released on every path. <sub>NCodeGroup maintainer: gap-hunting-review; NCodeGroup maintainer: principal-engineer-review; project-template .claude/commands/review-code.md</sub>
- **Validate a value at the API call that accepts it for deferred processing, so a bad value throws at its caller rather than during a later background flush; and after validating a creation request, pass the validated parameters on whole instead of re-deriving them from the raw request.** A bad value otherwise fails at every flush far from its source, and re-derived parameters may differ from what was validated. *Check:* Look for record or enqueue methods without eager argument validation, and handlers that rebuild sizes, curves or types from the raw request after validation. <sub>Identity ADR-1199; Identity ADR-1398</sub>
- **Don't refuse to start a host because configuration makes one stored item or one optional asset invalid (such as a missing static bundle); report the item and let it fail alone, for example with 503 for the missing asset.** One bad item would otherwise stop every replica and every tenant. *Check:* Look for startup validation that throws based on individual stored records or optional files instead of reporting them. <sub>Identity ADR-1412; Identity ADR-1438</sub>
- **Check a dependency that needs request services when the component uses it, not at startup, and when it is missing throw an `InvalidOperationException` whose message names the registration that fixes it.** A request-scoped dependency can't be built before a request exists, and the message tells the host how to fix its registration. *Check:* Look for startup or `IValidateOptions` checks that resolve scoped services, and type checks that fail with a generic message or not at all. <sub>Identity ADR-1238</sub>
- **When a job has several handlers, run them all even when one fails, and reschedule the job at most once per attempt.** Per-handler retries would rerun one failed attempt once for every failing handler. *Check:* Look for reschedule calls inside a per-handler loop or catch, or loops that exit on the first handler exception. <sub>Identity ADR-1242</sub>
- **When a request has no remote address, skip the address-based limit instead of failing the request, and log a warning once per process.** Socket and in-process test hosts have no remote address by design; the warning tells the operator the limit is off. *Check:* Look for limiters that throw or refuse on a null remote address, or skip silently or log on every request. <sub>Identity ADR-1399</sub>
- **In OAuth and OpenID Connect endpoints, use the error the specifications define for each refusal: `unsupported_response_type` for a response type the server or tenant doesn't support and `unauthorized_client` for one the client isn't allowed; `invalid_request` for a refusal the client can avoid by changing its request and `server_error` (HTTP 500) for a server configuration that cannot be satisfied.** RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1 defines distinct errors, and the client must tell its own error from a configuration error. *Check:* Check which error code each refusal path returns, and flag configuration-caused failures reported as `invalid_request` or request-caused ones reported as `server_error`. <sub>Identity ADR-1141; Identity ADR-1158</sub>
- **Validate PKCE `code_challenge` and `code_verifier` values as 43 to 128 characters drawn only from `[A-Za-z0-9-._~]`, on the server and where a client creates the verifier.** RFC 7636 §4.1 fixes this syntax. *Check:* Look for PKCE handling that skips the length or character-set check. <sub>Identity ADR-1144; Identity ADR-1275</sub>
- **Refuse client registration metadata the server cannot honor with `invalid_client_metadata` at registration: algorithm values outside the effective `*_values_supported`, an `*_enc` without its `*_alg`, an encrypted response without exactly one of `jwks`/`jwks_uri`, a capability discovery marks unsupported (such as `frontchannel_logout_uri` while `frontchannel_logout_supported` is false), a pairwise client with multi-host `redirect_uris` and no `sector_identifier_uri`, and an authentication method without the material it verifies against (`jwks`/`jwks_uri` for `private_key_jwt`, certificates for `self_signed_tls_client_auth`, exactly one `tls_client_auth_*` parameter for `tls_client_auth` and none for other methods). - **Once a JWT client assertion handler has claimed an assertion, make every refusal a conclusive `invalid_client` that the failed-authentication limiter counts; never defer to another handler after claiming.** A failed assertion must not fall through to another handler or escape the limiter. *Check:* Look for post-ownership failures that return 'undefined', use another error code, or skip the limiter. <sub>Identity ADR-1102</sub>
- **When a JWE content-key unwrap fails with `CryptographicException`, `JoseException` or `ArgumentException`, substitute a random content key, and in a loop over recipients or keys move to the next one only for those failures. - **Answer a refresh whose spend finds the grant missing or no longer active, including a spend lost to a concurrent request, exactly like reuse of a revoked refresh token: `invalid_grant`, apply the reuse policy and revoke the token family. - **Make a token validator return an invalid token as data (validity, a failure code and a reason), valid only when every requirement succeeded and no handler recorded a failure, with all failures aggregated. - **In a protocol client, return an OAuth error response (a JSON object with a string `error`, at any status) as a value; throw a protocol exception wrapping the cause for transport, timeout, size, JSON or malformed-response failures; classify an unreachable provider as one shared 'provider unavailable' failure; and throw `InvalidOperationException` for configuration errors.** Callers need errors like `invalid_grant` as values, while real failures and misconfiguration must be exceptions they can tell apart. *Check:* Look for code that throws on OAuth error responses, drops the inner exception, uses different failure codes for an unavailable provider, or uses a protocol exception for a configuration error. <sub>Identity ADR-1285; Identity ADR-1290</sub>
- **When DPoP or another binding is required but cannot be used, throw before sending anything: `InvalidOperationException` for client configuration (no key, an empty key ring, an unknown pinned key) and a provider exception when the provider advertises no usable algorithm.** A required binding must never fall back to an unbound request. *Check:* Look for required-binding paths that send the request without a proof or throw the wrong exception kind. <sub>Identity ADR-1286</sub>

- **Don't discover a key's format or family by trying parsers in turn and catching their exceptions; dispatch on the explicitly named format, key type and encoding, compared ordinally against the formats the key type declares.** Trial parsing relies on exception control flow and leaves the stored form ambiguous. *Check:* Look for try/catch chains that fall back from one import method (such as `ImportSubjectPublicKeyInfo`) to another when it throws, and for case-insensitive format-name comparison. <sub>Identity ADR-1104</sub>

- **Refuse with `invalid_grant` an approved device-authorization or CIBA grant whose payload lacks the subject's recorded authentication.** The subject can only be validated from its recorded authentication. *Check:* Look for handlers that continue or use a default when the subject authentication is null. <sub>Identity ADR-1225</sub>

- **Make session revalidation for a long-lived connection or circuit fail closed: keep looping and retry while the store is only temporarily unavailable, sign the user out and log on any other unexpected failure, let the loop's own cancellation end it, and keep the interval at most half the session's idle timeout. When a client probe gets a success status with a malformed body, treat it as unknown and keep the current state.** A connection must not stay signed in after its session ended or can't be verified, while a store outage or a proxy error page must not sign everyone out. *Check:* Look for revalidation catches that keep the user signed in or end the loop on unexpected errors, treat store unavailability as session end, swallow cancellation, and options that allow an interval over half the idle timeout; and for probe readers that return signed-out on `JsonException`. <sub>Identity ADR-1435; Identity ADR-1441; Identity outcomes of #600</sub>
- **Return anti-forgery and authentication refusals from a cookie-authenticating backend as RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable URN `type`, `title` and `status` and `Cache-Control: no-store`, audit each anti-forgery rejection, and make logout idempotent by redirecting when no session exists.** Clients tell failures apart by stable types, refusals must never be cached, and a second logout click must do no harm. *Check:* Look for plain-text or empty refusals, missing `type` or `no-store`, unaudited rejections, and logout handlers that error when the session is gone. <sub>Identity ADR-1292; Identity ADR-1293</sub>
- **When calling a key management service, map to a refusal (`CryptographicException`, then 400 with the reason) only the status that means a wrong key, ciphertext or context (for example HTTP 400 or gRPC `InvalidArgument`) and an unreadable key identifier (`ArgumentException`); throw `IOException` for an integrity failure (checksum mismatch, a response naming another key, version or algorithm); and let every other failure propagate, answering 502 after logging it with the provider and secret identifiers.** An outage or authorization failure must never be mistaken for a wrong key, and the type tells callers whether a retry is worth it. *Check:* Look for KMS catches that turn every failure into a refusal, treat refusals as 502 or upstream failures as 400, return 500, or log without the identifiers. <sub>Identity ADR-1260; Identity ADR-1474; Identity ADR-1476</sub>
- **When a nested revocation check of a signer or responder is not `Good`, treat the data it vouches for as unusable, never as `Revoked`.** An undetermined signer status is not evidence that the certificate is revoked. *Check:* Look for nested check failures propagated as `Revoked` for the original certificate. <sub>Identity ADR-1259</sub>
- **In a script, treat only a definite 'not found' as absent (such as an HTTP 404 from the structured status, or `git ls-remote --exit-code` returning 2), and stop with the tool's error on any other failure (auth, 5xx, network, missing ref). For `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, only exit 1 means 'not an ancestor'. Treat only a definite answer as a negative result, otherwise report 'unknown' and skip the action.** Reading every failure as 'no' or 'missing' leads to wrong reports or destructive steps, such as deleting a branch, on an answer the check never gave. *Check:* Look for existence probes, lookups and ancestry checks tested only as zero vs non-zero, failure branches that leave a flag at its false default and act on it, and output redirected to null before branching. <sub>project-template outcomes of #129; project-template outcomes of #146; project-template outcomes of #291; project-template outcomes of #310; project-template outcomes of #326; Identity review of #420</sub>
- **In a script, check `$?` and `$LASTEXITCODE` after every native command whose failure matters, cleanup and rollback commands included, and throw (or, for rollback, warn naming what was left behind and how to remove it) with the failed command and its key arguments. Print success only after every such command passed.** Native commands report failure only through exit codes, so the script otherwise reports success and the problem appears later as a confusing symptom. *Check:* Look for external tool calls followed by a success line without exit-code checks, and rollback commands piped to `Out-Null` with no check. <sub>project-template outcomes of #283; project-template outcomes of #291</sub>
- **Capture an external tool's stderr and include it (its first line, with no token or URL text) in the reported failure instead of redirecting it to `$null`, and never merge stderr into output parsed as a response body (`2>&1` before `ConvertFrom-Json`).** Without stderr a maintainer can't tell auth, DNS, not-found or network failures apart, and a warning on stderr corrupts JSON from a successful call. *Check:* Look for `2>$null` or discarded stderr followed by generic failure messages, and `2>&1` feeding a structured parse. <sub>project-template outcomes of #147; project-template outcomes of #225; project-template outcomes of #129</sub>
- **Don't map a failure to read, parse or measure input to a value that looks like valid content (an empty string, an empty collection, 0 cost, a success body that is empty, `null`, a scalar or an array). Return a distinct failure or 'unknown', warn naming the input, and don't publish or overwrite good output with it.** Callers can't tell unreadable input from empty input, so results built from incomplete data are reported as successful, such as a costly run reported as free. *Check:* Look for catches, `2>$null` or `$LASTEXITCODE` branches that set '' or 0 and continue, parsed responses used without null and shape checks after a success status, and missing tests for empty and non-JSON bodies. <sub>project-template outcomes of #331; project-template outcomes of #272; project-template outcomes of #147; project-template outcomes of #225</sub>
- **In PowerShell, pass an indexed or member-access value to a native command as a subexpression inside a quoted argument (`"body=$($map[$id])"`), never as `$map[$id]` or `$obj.Member` written directly.** Native command arguments expand only a bare variable, so the command receives the type name followed by literal text. *Check:* Look at native command arguments containing `$var[...]` or `$var.Prop` outside `$( )`. *Applies to:* `**/*.ps1` <sub>Identity powershell.instructions.md</sub>
- **In PowerShell, read a line that may be missing or empty as `"$(Get-Content -LiteralPath $path -TotalCount 1)".Trim()` or test for `$null` first, rather than calling a method directly on `Get-Content` output.** For an empty file `Get-Content` returns `$null`, so `.Trim()` throws before the script's own validation can report it. *Check:* Look for `(Get-Content ...).Trim()` or other method calls on possibly empty `Get-Content` output. <sub>project-template outcomes of #147</sub>
- **When an automation script applies several changes to an external system, run steps that can be refused before steps that write lasting state, make sure the condition that says an action is needed and the code that performs it treat a missing value the same way, and when an expected sub-object of an existing resource is missing, report it rather than writing invented defaults.** A late failure leaves a half-configured system that later runs skip, a missing field can be counted as needed and then silently skipped, and invented defaults overwrite settings the owner chose. *Check:* Look for fallible calls after writes that make later runs skip them, `-ne` conditions followed by a separate truthiness test on a derived value, and fallback branches that build full parameter sets from literals for an update. <sub>project-template outcomes of #140; project-template outcomes of #222</sub>
- **When judging whether an existing setting already satisfies a requirement, test it against the same full set of requirements the code holds its own setting to.** A narrower check reports 'already set' while other required items stay unmet. *Check:* Look for two paths judging the same kind of setting where one checks the full list and the other a single hard-coded item. <sub>project-template outcomes of #331</sub>
- **Make a best-effort delete that ignores errors check afterwards whether the target still exists, and report its path if it does.** A locked file otherwise leaves the folder behind without anyone being told. *Check:* Look for `Remove-Item -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` or a delete in a swallowed try/catch with no later existence check. <sub>project-template outcomes of #144</sub>
- **Make a hand-written parser for a standard format (such as YAML) accept every valid form of the construct it reads, with a test per form; and make code that writes a binary format by hand decode its output with an independent decoder and stop if it differs.** An unhandled valid form silently yields no results, and a wrong header field shows up only when a consumer fails to load the file. *Check:* Look for line-based parsers with indentation assumptions that reject valid forms, and hand-built binary writers that never read back their bytes. <sub>project-template outcomes of #331; project-template outcomes of #335</sub>
- **When truncating sections to fit a size limit and reporting what was omitted, handle the case where even the first (newest) item doesn't fit with its own accurate message.** Otherwise the newest item is described as 'older', the count is wrong, and it is never shown. *Check:* Look for truncation loops that can stop at index 0 and still emit an 'N older items omitted' message, and for a missing test with one oversized item. <sub>project-template outcomes of #147</sub>
- **In a shell script that installs packages with `apt-get`, run `apt-get update` before the install, or retry the install once after `apt-get update` when it fails.** In a container with empty or stale apt lists the install can't pull dependencies. *Check:* Look for `apt-get install` with no preceding update and no retry after one. <sub>project-template outcomes of #282</sub>
- **In a Helm chart, make the templates `fail` at render time for values that are mutually exclusive, incomplete, or have no effect on their own (a dependent value set while its feature is disabled, a half-set credential or identity, a required Secret key left empty), and for any combination that would make the workload verify TLS against a CA that didn't sign its certificate. Name the value the operator must set.** The chart should refuse any release the host would refuse, before anything is deployed, instead of installing cleanly and failing at runtime. *Check:* When a chart adds alternative, dependent, required or TLS/CA values, check that the templates validate the combinations and call `fail` with a message naming the value. <sub>Identity ADR-1485; Identity ADR-1506; Identity ADR-1509; Identity outcomes of #795</sub>
- **Constrain every OpenTofu input whose valid values are narrower than its type with a `validation` block whose `error_message` names the variable and states what it must be.** Invalid inputs should fail at plan time with a clear message, not at apply or in the provider. *Check:* Look for variables with restricted values (enums, formats, ranges, lengths) without `validation`, or messages that don't name the variable and requirement. *Applies to:* `**/*.tf`, `**/*.tftest.hcl` <sub>identity-platform opentofu.instructions.md</sub>
- **In an edit form for an existing resource, prefill every stored field the submission sends.** Otherwise changing one field silently clears or changes the others. *Check:* Compare the form's initial values with the fields of its submitted request body and the stored resource. <sub>Identity outcomes of #584</sub>
- **Don't report a brute-force, replay or failed-attempt limiter for failing closed (letting its store's exceptions propagate without a breaker or limiter-specific timeout); only a capacity guard such as a request-rate limit must fail open.** Failing open would lift the security control during a store outage, exactly when an attacker can cause one. *Check:* Before reporting, check whether the limiter guards correctness or capacity. <sub>Identity outcomes of #547</sub>
- **Don't report an audit or event publish awaited after a commit as able to fail the response when the publisher's contract isolates handler faults and sibling endpoints record their audit the same way.** A throwing handler never aborts the publish or the caller under that contract. *Check:* Before reporting, read the publisher's documented fault-isolation contract and how sibling write endpoints audit after the commit. <sub>Identity outcomes of #553</sub>
- **Don't report a deviation from a general error-handling rule when a decision record the code or feature cites explicitly records it (for example counting a final lost concurrency race as failed so a later pass retries it).** The deviation is intended and documented. *Check:* Before reporting, search the decision records the code cites for one covering the behaviour. <sub>Identity outcomes of #553</sub>
- **Don't report a missing or changed `InnerException` as a compatibility break when the thrown type is unchanged, no underlying exception remains to wrap, and the message carries the diagnostic details.** Callers catch by type, which still works, and nothing diagnostic is lost. *Check:* Check whether the thrown type changed and whether a real underlying exception exists before flagging. <sub>Identity outcomes of #460</sub>
- **Don't ask to move an inline, entity-specific validation check into a shared validator when that validator serves other entity types with different requirements, a lower layer already enforces the rule for every caller, and the inline check only maps it to a precise error response.** Moving it would impose one entity's limit on others; the inline check exists only to return a precise 400. *Check:* Before reporting duplication, check the shared validator's other callers and whether a lower layer already enforces the rule. <sub>Identity outcomes of #463</sub>
- **Don't flag case-insensitive deduplication or comparison of identifiers as a bug when the stores key those identifiers by a normalized form and match them case-insensitively.** Ids differing only by case name the same entity there. *Check:* Before reporting a comparer mismatch, check how the store keys and normalizes the identifier. <sub>Identity outcomes of #585</sub>
- **Don't report an endpoint filter's `Response.StatusCode >= 400` guard for failed binding as unreachable: with `RouteHandlerOptions.ThrowOnBadRequest` off, minimal APIs set 400 on a binding failure and still run the filter pipeline.** The guard does fire in a non-throwing host. *Check:* Before flagging the guard, check whether the host can run with `ThrowOnBadRequest` off and whether a test sends a value that fails to bind. <sub>Identity outcomes of #710</sub>
- **Don't ask to narrow a remote key provider's mapping of a decrypt HTTP 400 or gRPC `InvalidArgument` to `CryptographicException` when the provider verifies a key's operations and algorithm before storing it and the service reports disabled or deleted keys with other statuses that propagate.** For a stored, verified key the only remaining cause of that status is the service refusing the ciphertext. *Check:* Before reporting, check whether create and bind paths verify the key and which statuses the service uses for disabled or missing keys. <sub>Identity outcomes of #702</sub>
- **Don't report an existence check (such as `Test-Path`) on a path listed by `git worktree list` as redundant.** Git still lists prunable worktrees whose folders were deleted. *Check:* Before flagging an existence check as redundant, see whether its path comes from a listing that can include stale entries. <sub>project-template outcomes of #354</sub>
